sections.heading: Cost classification and behaviour in Cost and Management Accounting
paragraphs: Cost classification and behaviour is studied here as a specific part of Cost and Management Accounting. Begin by defining the term precisely and identifying the problem it helps explain or solve. Keep the scope narrow: related ideas may interact with it, but they are not interchangeable.

Accounting records and communicates financial effects of transactions. The accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Double-entry recording means each transaction affects at least two accounts so total debits equal total credits; this arithmetic equality does not, by itself, prove that every transaction is correct or complete.

examples.title: Worked application: Cost-volume-profit analysis
steps: Cost-volume-profit analysis models the relationship among selling price, variable cost, fixed cost, volume, and profit. Contribution per unit equals selling price minus variable cost per unit. Break-even units equal fixed costs divided by contribution per unit, assuming constant prices/cost behaviour and a relevant range.
Identify the assumption or condition on which the explanation depends.
Apply the same principle to a changed case and state what would change in the result.
Write a conclusion that answers the question directly and notes one relevant limitation.
examples.note: Original Student Plug teaching example; not an official university solution or verified past examination question.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A product sells for ₦5,000 and has variable cost ₦3,000 per unit. What is its contribution per unit?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Contribution per unit is selling price minus variable cost: ₦5,000−₦3,000=₦2,000.

examples.title: Worked application: Budget preparation and variance
steps: A budget is a quantified plan for a defined period. A variance is the difference between a recorded outcome and a budget or standard; whether it is favourable depends on the item and its effect on profit or objectives. Variance analysis should investigate causes, controllability, and whether the original budget assumptions remain relevant.
Identify the assumption or condition on which the explanation depends.
Apply the same principle to a changed case and state what would change in the result.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Why should a favourable cost variance still be investigated?
options: It may result from lower quality, delayed activity, or an unrealistic budget
Favourable always means every objective was achieved
It removes the need for future budgets
practiceQuestions.explanation: A numerical variance needs context; underspending may reflect efficiency or failure to deliver planned work.
